title: Granny's Garden
build: TOSEC disc, Granny's Garden (1983)(4Mation)[GRAN1].ssd (SHA-256 71511f3f...0d60f0), a DFS disc of two BBC BASIC II programs, GRAN1 and GRAN2, both saved from &0E00; analysed at PAGE &0E00, where each part's own relocation (lines 3280 and 2590) puts it

records.c: Line 100. Its bytes are a statement as BASIC tokenises one, PAGE and GOTO as tokens and 3280 as a line number (&8D), which the tokeniser never does after a REM typed in; but the first byte, at &0E04, is REM (&F4), written by line 110's poke. Before the poke the line sent a program loaded anywhere but &0E00 to the relocation at line 3280 (most likely `IF PAGE<>&E00 GOTO3280`; the token the poke replaced is lost). Now it does nothing, so CHAIN leaves the program where it loads.

Line 110, `CLEAR:?&E04=244`: forgets the variables and writes the REM token over line 100's first byte, so that later RUNs (ON ERROR RUN, PROCkey) do not test PAGE again; the RUN which ends the relocation has made its test already, at line 100, before it reaches this line. In this copy the byte is 244 already.

Lines 120-130: two REMs, `GRANNY'S GARDEN (C) 4MAT 1983` and `MIKE MATSON`, each after a quotation mark and a teletext colour code (&82 green, &85 magenta), so that LIST in Mode 7 shows them in colour.

Line 140, `ON ERROR RUN`: every error the program does not trap starts Part 1 again from line 100. That is how the game gets out of BASIC's Too many REPEATs, met at the 20th visit to the hallway (the 19th after a malformed tree guess, which leaves PROCtr's REPEAT at line 300 open), and Too many GOSUBs, met first on some routes: each trip up the stairs once the snake is dead leaves two GOSUBs open (lines 1610 and 1710). `No room` cannot be trapped and stops the program.

Line 150: `VDU 23;8202;0;0;0;` is VDU 23,0,10,32,0,0,0,0,0,0, which writes 32 to the CRTC's register 10, turning the cursor off (jsbeeb src/video.js reads bits 5 and 6 of R10, and 1 there never shows it); VDU 26 restores the default windows, 12 clears the screen, 15 turns paged mode off. `*FX11,0` sets the auto-repeat delay to 0, which turns auto-repeat off.

Lines 160-200: Part 1's variables and the sentences several scenes share. Z counts the children a password says are found (0-3), so name$(Z) is the next to look for; stick%, cup%, ap% and snake% are TRUE once the stick is taken, the cupboard has been visited, the apple is taken and the snake is dead; try counts the snake's misses (the tree puzzle leaves it at 1); bf and be are 1 once the butterfly and the bee have been hurt in the wood, bee once the bee has chased the dog, v once the spider has helped. f$ is five solid graphics blocks (&FF) for the pictures; lv$, g$, m$, s$, l$, j$, n$, b5$, b7$, h$, i$, w$, y$, x$, p$, r$, u$, v$ and q3$-q8$ are sentences the scenes print.

Lines 220-240, the first screen, `Ready to start?`, asked until the answer begins with Y. on% (music on) is set TRUE and t% FALSE once, before the loop. An answer ending in f sets on% FALSE: no tune at the title or in the kingdom, and the witch comes silently. One beginning with T sets t%, which puts the magic tree at a1 (line 290). The field takes four letters, and the key after the fourth, RETURN included, deletes it (PROCi), so `Yf` works and `Yesf` cannot be given.
Line 250, the title: `Granny's Garden` and `Part 1` in double height between two rows of 37 asterisks, then the theme tune (PROCsnd1) if on%.

Line 260, the whole of Part 1: a pause (PROCp(6)), the magic trees (PROCtr) and the Kingdom of the Mountains (PROCkn). Every way the kingdom can end RUNs the program again, through PROCkey or through ON ERROR RUN after Too many REPEATs or GOSUBs (`No room` stops it), so END is never reached.

PROCtr, the magic trees (lines 270-300). Line 280 numbers the rows 3, 2 and 1 down the left, builds tr$, one tree as Mode 7 graphics, from the 59 values of lines 2330-2340 (each plus 160; -150 becomes a line feed and -152 a backspace, so the string draws on several rows), and prints it twelve times: four columns, 9 apart, by three rows, 6 apart. Line 290 letters the columns a-d, sets a text window below the trees and chooses the tree: column L=RND(3)*9+4, so 13, 22 or 31 (b, c, d), and row M=RND(2)*6, so 6 or 12 (rows 2 and 1). Column a and row 3 are never chosen, except that t% (T at Ready to start?) puts it at a1 (4, 12). Line 300 sets try=0 and calls PROCtx until the guess is the tree.

PROCtx, one guess at the tree (lines 310-430). Each time it says `There is a magic tree here.`, and the first time (try=0) waits for the space bar after it; it asks `Which one do you think it is?` with INPUT, the only INPUT in Part 1, and sets try=1. The answer is lowercased (PROClcase). More than two characters gets `Please try again.` (line 440); a first character below A, a digit say, gets `Please put the letter first.` (line 450); a letter outside a-d or a second character outside 1-3 gets `Please try again.` too. The letter and digit become a column and a row through the tables at lines 2350 and 2360, and that tree flashes (lines 400-410). A wrong tree gets `There is not enough magic in that tree` and PROCtx calls itself, so it returns only when the guess is right.

PROCw(kk1,kk2,cl,q$), a room's frame: a clear screen, rows 0-3 in background colour kk1 and rows 5-24 in kk2, q$ as the heading in colour cl, and a text window from row 3 down. The second PROCb's last line feed comes on the bottom row and scrolls the screen up a row, so the bands end one row higher than they are written (in the hallway the CRTC starts the screen at &7C28, one row on). The hallway and each room use it.

PROCup: the cursor to the bottom row, then eight line feeds with a pause between, so the screen scrolls up eight rows: the raven at the top goes off it, and at line 2810 the toadstool drawn below the raven comes up to the top and stays.

PROCi(col,x,y,len) (lines 1020-1090), the game's own input, in double height in colour col at column x of row y. *FX15,0 first; then only letters, DELETE and RETURN count, so no answer holds a space or a digit. The first letter is shown as a capital and the rest in lower case, and in$ is built the same way, which is why the game matches lower-case fragments (`itch`, `rs`). When the cursor reaches column len the next key, whatever it is, is taken as DELETE: the field holds len-x-1 letters, and a letter beyond that is shown and then lost. A DELETE in an empty field still counts: l falls to -1 and stays one short of the letters shown, and LEFT$ with a length below 0 gives the whole string, so from then on each DELETE takes a letter too many off in$, or none, and in$ is not what the screen shows (live: DELETE, X, DELETE, Y shows Y and gives XY).

records.c: PROCsnd1 (lines 3200-3220), the theme tune: 103 steps read from line 3230, a pitch n and, when n>0, a length t (t=1 when n is 0), 155 values in all. Each length is divided by 1.5 and SOUND takes its whole part, so a step with n=0 is 0 long; A=(n+5)*4. Each step is three SOUNDs: channel 1 at A+96 and -12, given as &00011, whose flush digit plays each note at once and cuts off the one before; channel 2 at A and channel 3 at A+48, at -15, or at volume 0 when n is 0. Channel 1 runs ahead of the other two, which BASIC waits for (facts.md, Sound).
Lines 3230-3240, DATA: the theme tune for PROCsnd1, pitch and length pairs with 0 for a rest.

PROCsnd2 (lines 3250-3260), the kingdom's tune: fifteen notes, each RND(10)+10 long and the last 30, at a=(RND(10)+22)*4: channel 2 at a and -13 (&012, flushed), channel 3 at a+48 and -15, and channel 1 at a+32 and -12, given as &00111, whose synchronise digit holds each note for a note on another channel that never comes, so channel 1 is never heard (facts.md, Sound).
Line 3270, `PRINT ERR:PRINT ERL`: after PROCsnd2's ENDPROC, and no GOTO or GOSUB names it, so it never runs; most likely left from testing.

Lines 3280-3320, the relocation that line 100 no longer reaches: `*TAPE`, the program copied four bytes at a time from PAGE to &0E00, TOP's high byte (&13) lowered by the pages moved, PAGE set to &0E00, and RUN. The analysis runs it with `GOTO3280` after LOAD, which gives Part 1 the memory to be finished (orientation.md).
